transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
Hurricane Iscias has made landfall Friday night as a Category 2 hurricane with 105 mile-an-hour winds,
and it's now moving into Alabama.
Life-threatening storm surge and devastating winds meanwhile are being seen along the Florida panhandle
and Alabama coasts, and President Trump has declared an emergency for several counties in Alabama.
Troy Public Radio's Kyle Gassett reports.
Ahead of the storm, Alabama Governor Kay Ivey closed state offices
and ordered tourists to evacuate counties near the Gulf Coast.
She also urged Alabamians to stay weather-aware.
We often hear in emergency management, hope for the best, prepare for the worst.
That is the approach we need with this particular storm system.
Ivey also declared a state of emergency in 40 counties, including the state capital, Montgomery.
The declaration also triggered Alabama's price gouging law,
making it illegal for businesses to sharply raise prices on gasoline and other essential goods during the emergency.
This comes as consumers are already paying more, on average, at the pump.
For NPR News, I'm Kyle Gassett in Montgomery, Alabama.
Hurricane Simon, meanwhile, is now approaching Mexico's coast.
It's now a Category 2 storm with sustained winds of almost 100 miles an hour.
A hurricane warning has been issued for parts of Mexico's coasts.
Survivors of the 2009 shooting at Fort Hood Military Base in Texas
are speaking out after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced plans Friday
to livestream the execution of former Army Major Nidal Hassan.
Hassan was convicted of the massacre.
Sergeant Alonzo Lunsford was shot seven times.
He says while he wants Hassan to die, he doesn't want it to become a public spectacle.
We're not a nation that has every Thursday we're going to have a stoning.
For every Tuesday we're going to have a lashing or a beheading.
We're not doing that. We're better than that.
President Trump wrapped up a busy week of campaigning with a rally in Syracuse, New York Friday night.
The president made his pitch to voters on why they should support Republicans,
even though the party is facing major voter blowback in the final weeks of voting.
And Pierre's Deepa Shivram has more on our story.
Trump's message to New York voters was to argue that if Democrats win control of Congress, prices would go up.
He specifically focused on energy prices and his remarks in Syracuse that lasted more than 90 minutes
and wound through topics like lamenting that he did not get awarded the Nobel Peace Prize again.
Trump painted a rosy picture of the U.S. economy, despite the fact that polling shows that voters disapprove of the president's handling of it.
Trump also repeated a plea that he's been making to voters to "pretend that he's on the ballot" in an effort to try and drum up turnout.
Deepa Shivram, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Thousands of Indian security forces have shut down central New Delhi and they've detained protest leaders as authorities prevent protests against a controversial revision of electoral rolls that has seen millions struck off voter lists.
M.P.A.'s Diya Hadid reports.
Police boarded a flight that had just landed carrying protest leaders.
One leader, Abhijit Deepke, says in a video he shared online...
The police is here to arrest us.
Police also drag barricades across roads that lead to a protest site.
This bled over a loudspeaker.
Attention please, attention please, gathering here, taking out the procession is not allowed.
Police say they're preventing disorder.
The protests are over a controversial revision of voter rolls that has crossed millions of people off electoral lists.
Critics allege the government is trying to disenfranchise voters who are unlikely to vote for the ruling Hindu Nationalist Party led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The government has not responded to those accusations.
Diya Hadid, NPR News, New Delhi.
Kayla Thornton scored 18 points Friday night as the Golden State Valkyries became the quickest expansion to ever reach the WNBA Finals.
They swept the Las Vegas Aces 87-77 in overtime. The dream also swept New York Friday.
Angel Rescored 22 points as the dream won 85-83.
The four-seated dream haven't lost a game during this year's postseason play.
Golden State and Atlanta will play in the WNBA Finals with the first game on October 17th.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Hurricane Iscias makes landfall in Alabama as Category 2, Gov. Ivey declares emergencies
Hurricane Simon approaches Mexico's coast as Category 2 storm, hurricane warnings issued
Fort Hood shooting survivors speak out against Hegseth's plan to livestream Nidal Hassan execution
Trump rallies in Syracuse, New York, urging voters to back Republicans over price concerns
Indian security forces shut down New Delhi, detain leaders protesting voter roll revisions
Golden State Valkyries sweep Las Vegas Aces in overtime, reach WNBA Finals against Atlanta
